alignments.note: Genitive absolute participle expanded into a finite clause; the supplied when is its helper (rule 86), the particle against realizes the preverb of ἀντιλέγω and the supplied object it completes the verb's English (rules 7, 106). Discontinuous around the expressed subject. Head on the verb word spake.
Passive verb with its subject and auxiliary; head on constrained (rule 17).

Infinitive with its marker; ἐπικαλέω governs the accusative Καίσαρα, and an accusative has no case for an English preposition to realize, so unto is the verb's own phrasal government and stays inside its unit (rules 21, 106). Head on appeal.
Καίσαρα → Caesar, a bare accusative object (rule 106).
ὡς introducing the disclaimer clause → that (rule 40: a subordinating element is realized by whatever word introduces its English clause).

Participle rendered as a finite clause with its supplied subject; the supplied object whereof stays with the verb that requires it in English, exactly as rule 74 records for ἔχω. Discontinuous under rule 15. Head on had.
Infinitive with its marker (rules 7, 40). Head on accuse.
The determiner slot is occupied by my, which belongs to μου, so the article realizes nothing (rule 20).

review_notes: The variant unit is underdetermined on the base reading and every projected token is realized.
The placement of whereof follows rule 74's recorded corpus reading, which keeps the supplied object on ἔχω rather than on the infinitive.
